findings.title: Legacy recovery word reaches terminal scrollback outside the private screen
evidence: Local evidence: legacy-terminal-route.log (executed, exit 0); CLI SHA-256 c42e109da8fbccbb60a4646834fd5ced417e946e729359c6e38331c2941cab3a.
findings.reproduction: Run encode with the public BIP39 zero-entropy phrase, date 23-09-2026, seedshift-legacy and indexes. Redirect stdin from /dev/null and stdout to a file, leaving stderr attached to a non-dumb PTY.
findings.expected: Sensitive result lines use secret_channel and are never printed on an unprotected terminal.
findings.observed: The PTY received 'Word to remember: addict'. print_last_word selects Channel::Error based on redraw capability, not private-screen state.
findings.impact: The displaced masked word is recovery material. This is a confirmed partial-secret disclosure to scrollback, not disclosure of the entire seed or an assertion of remote compromise.
findings.recommendedFix: Route the complete legacy recovery-word section through the existing secret-output policy.
findings.requiredVerification: PTY tests with independently redirected stdin/stdout/stderr; assert no word appears outside the alternate screen, including error and cancellation paths.

findings.title: Unescaped discovered filenames can issue terminal control sequences
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Give a synthetic backup filename containing ESC[?1049l; collect it and present the resulting notice or choice in the terminal.
findings.expected: File paths are displayed as inert text; private-screen state cannot be changed by file content or names.
findings.observed: The executed collector assertion preserves the ESC byte. Static tracing finds no escaping before notice/choice rendering; ESC[?1049l is the terminal alternate-screen exit sequence. Private-screen bookkeeping is not updated by that sequence.
findings.impact: A specially named local or imported file can inject terminal control bytes into subsequent display. An actual emulator transition was not executed in this audit, nor was a remote delivery path or arbitrary code execution established.
findings.recommendedFix: Escape control characters in filesystem-derived display strings while keeping original paths for access.
findings.requiredVerification: Check single-result notices, multiple choices, nested folder names and control bytes; use a PTY to verify private-screen continuity.

findings.title: Public Debug implementations expose QR data and legacy recovery hints
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Create a QR PNG from a public fixture, admit it and format the result using Debug. Separately format Encoding and ShareUnmasking with known recovery words.
findings.expected: Diagnostic formatting redacts secret-bearing data.
findings.observed: Admitted derives Debug over its entire borrowed PNG. Encoding and ShareUnmasking also print the recovery-word index.
findings.impact: A caller's debug logging can preserve the full recoverable QR image. Automatic production logging was not established; the smaller hint exposure has the same redaction root cause.
findings.recommendedFix: Implement redacted Debug for secret-bearing public results and audit variants of the same pattern.
findings.requiredVerification: Normal and pretty Debug must omit bytes, reversible encodings and original_last_word/last_word values.

findings.title: Legacy embroidery and share producers discard the exact-recovery word
findings.reproduction: Create Original Seedshift backup, embroidery and SSKR shares for the same public phrase/date. Compare the returned or displayed original_last_word and restore a fixture with multiple valid candidates.
findings.expected: Every producer of checksum-corrected Original Seedshift retains and safely exposes the extra word needed to choose the original phrase.
findings.observed: Plain Backup::encode retains the word; written_entropy keeps only entropy and split_backup keeps shares/held phrase. Their CLI/binding results do not expose the discarded word.
findings.impact: Correct dates can leave multiple possible seeds; the heirs sheet assumes a word was supplied. Other wallet evidence can still distinguish candidates, so irreversible loss is not asserted.
findings.recommendedFix: Carry the recovery hint through all native and browser producer results and display it through the private-screen policy.
findings.requiredVerification: Round trip plain, share and embroidery outputs on a multi-candidate public fixture; the saved hint must uniquely recover the original.

findings.title: Folder collection drops different groups' same-numbered SSKR members
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Create two required groups, each 1-of-1, using deterministic public randomness. restore_complete accepts the two original shares. Add them through Collector and examine the result.
findings.expected: Identity is (group_index, member_index), and eligibility uses the complete SSKR topology.
findings.observed: Only member_index is used for deduplication; the last member_threshold determines apparent completeness. One of two required shares is dropped and the result can still appear complete.
findings.impact: An explicitly supported imported grouped set cannot be recovered through discovery despite a sufficient original quorum. Core restoration from the full explicit list remains available.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the core topology and identity rules; reject conflicting copies and inconsistent metadata explicitly.
findings.requiredVerification: Test multi-group thresholds, overlapping member numbers, identical duplicates, conflicting duplicates and permutations. Include browser collection.

findings.title: An incomplete surplus card share makes a sufficient set unavailable
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Collect complete card representations of two shares of a 2-of-3 set, plus an incomplete third share missing an internal card.
findings.expected: Determine recoverability from usable shares while reporting damaged surplus inputs separately.
findings.observed: The first card-part error is copied into set.trouble and excludes the entire set, regardless of the already available quorum.
findings.impact: Recovery is unnecessarily refused when all files are selected together. Selecting only the two complete shares is a workaround.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate per-share parse errors from set topology; do not discard integrity warnings or silently accept conflicting usable shares.
findings.requiredVerification: Two complete plus one incomplete must restore with a warning; an actually insufficient or inconsistent quorum must still refuse.

findings.title: A card word-count choice leaks into later input retries
findings.reproduction: Select 12 words for a card backup that fails validation, then use Read another file to supply a valid 24-word text backup without --words.
findings.expected: Replacing the input clears metadata belonging only to the previous selection.
findings.observed: The process-global CHOSEN_WORDS is reused for non-card input; the reader truncates the replacement to its leading codes.
findings.impact: Valid recovery input can fail or produce a misleading shorter candidate after a retry. The same input in a fresh process is unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Bind the count to the selected backup and clear it whenever that selection changes.
findings.requiredVerification: PTY regression for 12-to-24 and 24-to-12 replacements, text and QR inputs, including explicit --words.

findings.title: A wrong hint for the first share candidate aborts the remaining search
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Provide two restored synthetic legacy sets A and B, a last-word hint valid for B but incompatible with A, and the known dates. Compare B alone with [A,B].
findings.expected: A recovery hint rejects a candidate, not the entire multi-candidate search.
findings.observed: decode_with_last_word and Phrase::of_indexes errors propagate through ? from take_set before the next set is visited.
findings.impact: Candidate ordering prevents the correct recoverable seed from being found: B alone passes, while [A,B] returns Backup(LastWord), confirmed by the public-input harness.
findings.recommendedFix: Handle expected candidate mismatches locally; preserve genuine input/system errors.
findings.requiredVerification: Permute candidate order; wrong hint/checksum in early candidates must not suppress a later valid match.

findings.title: Re-encoding with the returned legacy mode drops the recovery hint
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Encode with SeedshiftLegacy, then encode the same phrase/dates with first.backup.mode().
findings.expected: Equivalent supported legacy modes return consistent recovery metadata.
findings.observed: Codes are identical, but the second Encoding.original_last_word is None because only SeedshiftLegacy is tested.
findings.impact: A library host reusing the returned mode loses the hint. Plain CLI selection does not directly select the internal variant.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat both legacy variants consistently or explicitly reject the unsupported producer mode.
findings.requiredVerification: Assert code and hint equivalence for both variants across all five phrase lengths.

findings.title: Serialized legacy records conflict with their own in-memory mode
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Encode legacy, serialize backup.record(), parse with BackupReading and pass backup.mode() to mode_conflict.
findings.expected: A record agrees with the algorithm of the backup that produced it.
findings.observed: Serialization uses seedshift-legacy for both variants, but enum equality reports Original Seedshift versus Original Seedshift as a conflict.
findings.impact: Library callers and backup checking can reject their own compatible records.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare serialized algorithm identity independently from inferred checksum state.
findings.requiredVerification: Both historical spellings and current headerless/headered records, positive and genuine mismatch cases.

findings.title: API migration leaves repository test targets uncompilable
findings.reproduction: Run cargo test --locked --offline --workspace --no-run; independently compile the cards and WASM tests.
findings.expected: All release-required test targets compile against the current APIs.
findings.observed: Constructor callers still use .unwrap() after a Self return, and several encode calls pass a removed fifth boolean. All three scoped attempts exited 101.
findings.impact: The release gate cannot execute its assertions. A successful executable build does not establish a passing workspace.
findings.recommendedFix: Migrate every test and helper to the new API without deleting assertions or excluding failing targets.
findings.requiredVerification: Workspace compile-only pass, then run migrated functional tests and the mandatory release gates.

findings.title: Regression tests still drive removed prompts and output contracts
findings.reproduction: Run the bounded CLI suites listed in the execution ledger.
findings.expected: Tests follow the current UI while preserving privacy and payload assertions.
findings.observed: Tests expect MNC1 legend output, an implicit QR sidecar and obsolete checklist/source/prompt order. Several PTY cases wait for their 180-second timeout.
findings.impact: Release regression coverage is broken and slow. These particular waits are stale test interactions, not evidence the application itself deadlocks.
findings.recommendedFix: Update prompt interactions and explicit --card-qr-png fixtures; keep separate assertions for deliberately absent sidecars and exact recovery.
findings.requiredVerification: Run each formerly failing case, then the bounded CLI suites with truthful timeouts and no mass-rendering tests.

findings.title: WASM ABI verifier retains the removed encode argument
findings.reproduction: Build a fresh phrase profile and run the documented backup ABI diagnostic on that exact module.
findings.expected: The typed ABI call matches the current wasm-bindgen export.
findings.observed: The verifier requests six i32 parameters including the removed boolean; the current four-JsValue function plus result pointer requires five.
findings.impact: The canonical verifier stops before its memory-cleanup assertions. This is not evidence of an actual memory leak; fresh wasm32 execution was not performed in this audit.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the typed call and its argument tuple, preserving both positive and negative diagnostic controls.
findings.requiredVerification: Fresh wasm32/glue generation and the ABI verifier, followed by its marker/cleanup controls.

findings.title: Architecture and refusal registries lag behind new modules
findings.reproduction: Run cargo xtask code-rules on the final source snapshot.
findings.expected: New modules, allowed dependencies, refusal IDs and size limits satisfy the enforced architecture.
findings.observed: Baseline reports 13 production failures. The retained final-source rerun reports 18: new modules/import edges, refusal IDs, the sha2 dependency and an 801-line PTY test. An interim harness lint-configuration error was corrected and is excluded.
findings.impact: Mandatory gates fail; input -> card_files -> input/commands also requires an actual layering decision, not merely adding names.
findings.recommendedFix: Register supported boundaries and refusal codes, remove the dependency cycle and split oversized source where appropriate.
findings.requiredVerification: Fresh code-rules with its self-test on the frozen tree; no broad allowlist bypass.

findings.title: New code introduces unacknowledged duplicate implementations
findings.reproduction: Run cargo xtask copies.
findings.expected: The duplication gate passes with shared helpers or narrowly justified intentional copies.
findings.observed: Baseline reports three pairs; moving collection removes one pair, leaving the parser/text and output/menu pairs in the later run.
findings.impact: Duplicated logic can drift and the required gate fails.
findings.recommendedFix: Consolidate shared behavior or document a genuinely necessary deliberate copy with its rationale.
findings.requiredVerification: copies plus copies --self-test on the final tree; preserve both callers' behavior.

findings.title: Shift+Tab resets choices in configured child commands
findings.reproduction: Select Original Seedshift in a configured child, reach Dates, press Shift+Tab and then Enter without selecting another mode.
findings.expected: Backtracking highlights the previously selected option.
findings.observed: Choice memory is initialized by the parent menu, but the fresh child enables backtracking without it; the default mode is selected.
findings.impact: The user can unknowingly switch masking algorithms on going back. Existing tests explicitly choose replacements and miss this case.
findings.recommendedFix: Initialize choice memory in the child or use the typed configuration as the source of the current selection.
findings.requiredVerification: PTY tests that go back and confirm unchanged choices for modes, forms and export options.

findings.title: --find silently accepts unknown values and falls back to other file kinds
findings.reproduction: Point --find cards at a folder containing only one normal backup QR; repeat with --find typo, noninteractively.
findings.expected: The documented filter is enforced and invalid values are rejected.
findings.observed: Unknown values become Any. If no requested kind exists, the collector offers/returns other kinds; a single result is consumed without explaining the fallback.
findings.impact: Automation can decode an unintended class of input contrary to help. The code does not establish secret corruption merely from this mismatch.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate values and enforce the filter; if interactive fallback is desired, ask explicitly and describe it.
findings.requiredVerification: Every valid kind, unknown kinds, empty matches, single and multiple alternatives in interactive and batch modes.

findings.title: Wrong-date success rates describe only the older uncorrected legacy format
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; 288 of 336 deliberately wrong dates gave at least one checksum-valid candidate (349 total) for one fixed synthetic 12-word backup. Not a population estimate.
findings.reproduction: Compare the stated 1-in-16 to 1-in-256 rate with checksum-corrected legacy candidates; enumerate a small fixed public fixture.
findings.expected: Rates distinguish historic legacy from the currently written checksum-corrected form, including whether a remembered word is known.
findings.observed: The prose assigns the old rate to Original Seedshift generally; current enumeration considers multiple displaced checksum bits, and the implementation's estimator assumes one candidate per date combination. The separate 288/336 result applies only to its fixed fixture.
findings.impact: Readers can overestimate the date filter's discrimination and underestimate wallet-check work.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe both legacy forms and the known-word condition. Treat the bounded fixture as a counterexample, not a population estimate.
findings.requiredVerification: Check all overview/help/manual statements against current candidate enumeration.

findings.title: Manual recovery examples still claim the legend reveals its masking mode
findings.reproduction: Compare the example's claimed 'marked as masked with Seedshift' output with the embedded helper and current Holds::Entropy format.
findings.expected: The manual explains that current entropy legends do not identify whether/how dates were used.
findings.observed: The example and its promised helper output still claim an intrinsic Seedshift mode marker; the current helper only states a conditional interpretation.
findings.impact: An heir can choose an incorrect reversal procedure from a format description that contradicts its own reader.
findings.recommendedFix: Update both manual copies and clearly mark the superseded ADR decision rather than rewriting history.
findings.requiredVerification: Execute the documented public example and compare exact output; keep source and exported manual identical.

findings.title: Product overview overstates platform isolation and exit cleanup
findings.reproduction: Compare unconditional network-closed and only-chosen-files statements with Windows protections and both publication/cleanup failure branches.
findings.expected: Overview promises have the same platform and failure qualifications as SECURITY.md.
findings.observed: Windows has no implemented unprivileged network/file-write sandbox. LeftStagingCopy follows successful publication with failed staging cleanup; FailedSaveLeftCopy covers a failed save that also leaves its staging copy.
findings.impact: Readers may mistake application behavior for an OS-enforced guarantee or assume no secret-bearing staging file survives, whether publication succeeded or failed.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify platform-dependent guarantees and both staging-remnant outcomes concisely, linking the security policy.
findings.requiredVerification: Review normal, cancellation, failed-publication and successful-publication/failed-cleanup branches against each public promise.

findings.title: Menu documentation retains removed display and standalone QR questions
findings.reproduction: Trace the current configured Encode/share/standalone QR menu against its documented sequence.
findings.expected: Menu instructions match the questions actually offered; flags and interactive capabilities are distinguished.
findings.observed: The guides still describe a separate disabled-by-default original-display choice and standalone QR contact/link/text submenu absent from the current flow.
findings.impact: Users cannot follow the written procedure and may confuse which phrase/result is displayed.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the affected sequences from the final flow; retain descriptions of still-supported CLI flags separately.
findings.requiredVerification: Walk each documented path and compare every question and default, including private-screen behavior.

findings.title: Piped-input examples fail when run in an ordinary terminal
findings.reproduction: Run the public piped mnemonic example while stdout/stderr remain attached to a terminal.
findings.expected: An example either works as shown or explicitly redirects output so the private-screen gate can admit it.
findings.observed: Piping stdin prevents terminal_available; terminal stdout requires a private screen. --output alone does not redirect stdout.
findings.impact: A recommended example fails before its advertised operation. The guard itself is appropriate.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a fully nonterminal pipeline or a local mnemonic file with the supported private-screen flow.
findings.requiredVerification: Execute every repaired README/help example with actual TTY channel combinations.

findings.title: Release notes overstate 0.1.0 write and interaction compatibility
findings.reproduction: Compare the broad compatibility statement with headerless output, removed legacy flags and current checksum-corrected producers.
findings.expected: Reading compatibility is distinguished from changed output formats and prompts.
findings.observed: The opening promises all old read/write behavior and unchanged commands/questions except a list that omits these changes.
findings.impact: Release users can misplan migration or scripted consumers.
findings.recommendedFix: Describe the actual input compatibility and breaking output/CLI changes, consistent with CHANGELOG.md.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare both flags and serialized outputs for documented old/current public fixtures.

findings.title: Coverage guide calls wasmi verification a browser execution
findings.reproduction: Trace the command described as executing binding entry points in a browser.
findings.expected: Evidence names the actual runtime and its integration boundary.
findings.observed: The command instantiates WASM under wasmi; it does not execute generated JavaScript in a browser.
findings.impact: Coverage is overstated at the JS/glue/DOM boundary. Historical percentages themselves are explicitly revision-bound and are not a defect.
findings.recommendedFix: Name wasmi and separately list real-browser coverage or its absence.
findings.requiredVerification: Cross-check coverage prose against retained commands and runtime versions.

findings.title: Architecture counts an internal legacy variant as a selectable mode
findings.reproduction: Compare the documented public registry with Mode::ALL.
findings.expected: Separate selectable modes from an internal checksum-state variant.
findings.observed: The architecture describes four public modes while the public list has three.
findings.impact: Hosts following the architecture can expose or count a nonselectable internal state.
findings.recommendedFix: Document three public algorithms and the separate internal legacy state.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare architecture, Rust registry, CLI and WASM selectors.

findings.title: Library guide claims an incomplete list of LegendEntropy constructors is exhaustive
findings.reproduction: Read the 'No other public way' statement and the public legend_entropy dispatcher.
findings.expected: The public API guide includes all supported construction entry points.
findings.observed: legend_entropy is public but absent from the exhaustive list.
findings.impact: Library integrators are directed away from the shared dispatcher.
findings.recommendedFix: Document the dispatcher or remove the exhaustive assertion; avoid duplicating detailed signatures.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile the documented minimal call using the current public interface.

findings.title: Share export documentation uses the folder collision suffix for files too
findings.reproduction: Compare filename and directory collision handling with name-1 in the guide.
findings.expected: File and directory names are described accurately.
findings.observed: Files use an underscore suffix and folders use a hyphen suffix.
findings.impact: Scripts or users looking for the promised output name can miss it.
findings.recommendedFix: State the two naming policies or describe automatic numbering without a false universal spelling.
findings.requiredVerification: One occupied-file and one occupied-directory synthetic example.

findings.title: Map provenance points to removed current generation commands
findings.reproduction: Compare the NOTICE's generator/data paths with the current Rust assets.
findings.expected: Historic provenance remains intact while current regeneration instructions resolve.
findings.observed: The notice names former Node/TypeScript generation paths; the Rust renderer consumes the bundled world-land resource instead.
findings.impact: A maintainer cannot reproduce the asset via the presented current instructions.
findings.recommendedFix: Label the historical generation chain and identify the current retained resource/provenance without inventing a regeneration step.
findings.requiredVerification: Resolve every current path and verify resource attribution/checksums.

findings.title: Native license companion omits MnemoCode's own attribution
findings.reproduction: Inspect native packaging and compare its license companion with LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE and NOTICE.
findings.expected: The native distribution includes its own attribution and applicable license text alongside dependency notices.
findings.observed: The companion copies THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES alone, whose generator excludes the project's own crates; artwork references license files not included in the native asset set.
findings.impact: Distribution documentation is incomplete. This audit makes no legal determination.
findings.recommendedFix: Include the project's attribution and applicable license text in the existing companion. MIT OR Apache-2.0 does not itself require two separately named files.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect a freshly assembled companion's exact content; retain the expected asset-count/provenance checks.

findings.title: Sheet and separate-card exports disagree on document identity
findings.reproduction: Export an ordinary public backup as a sheet and separate cards with several padding decoys, then collect both presentations.
findings.expected: The documented document ID stays the same for representations of one backup.
findings.observed: The sheet hashes all decoys; the separate layout keeps only the first decoy and hashes that different list. Discovery yields two ordinary-backup items.
findings.impact: Batch discovery can refuse with Several even though the files represent one backup. Same-layout files and SSKR grouping by share reference are not shown broken by this case.
findings.recommendedFix: Carry the original plan identity through layout transformation instead of recomputing it from shortened presentation data.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare sheet/separate IDs with one and multiple decoys, ordinary and SSKR outputs, without large render matrices.

findings.title: Browser embroidery shares still lack typed-legend recovery and pattern heirs
findings.reproduction: Take a textual legend from StitchShares.legend and restore it using the public browser API without enclosing it in a PDF/QR. Compare native share_of_legend. Inspect available heir-sheet variants.
findings.expected: Browser users can restore a printed share legend and generate its pattern-specific heir instructions, matching the supported native operations.
findings.observed: New StitchShares and file readers cover creation/file import, but readStitchLegend still uses the whole-phrase reader and rejects shares. HeirPage exposes encoded/shares sheets, not Pattern/PatternShares.
findings.impact: A browser can create recovery material whose handwritten legend it cannot consume through the supported API. File import is now present and must not be reported missing.
findings.recommendedFix: Expose typed share-legend conversion with correction metadata and the corresponding pattern heir operations.
findings.requiredVerification: One small native/browser 2-of-3 round trip from text and files; verify heir instructions and consumer integration. No exhaustive rendering matrix needed.

findings.title: File metadata guesses form and word count from an MNC1 header
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log; intended regression assertion failed while its public-fixture controls passed.
findings.reproduction: Read a public QR containing a valid 12-word MNC1:direct:indexes record; inspect codes_of and BackupFile.words.
findings.expected: Interpret the recorded form and count the record's payload, not its header.
findings.observed: Form::likely sees the whole record and labels it words; the browser getter passes that string into the form parser and returns None rather than 12.
findings.impact: Discovery labels and size hints are wrong for supported legacy record files; loss of the underlying recovered phrase is not established.
findings.recommendedFix: Parse the envelope before applying form detection and counting.
findings.requiredVerification: Headered/headerless forms and typed legends through the shared collector and browser getter.

findings.title: The new browser-files feature omits its direct optional cards dependency
evidence: Local evidence: files-feature-isolated.log; native isolated-feature cargo check exited 101 with E0433 at files.rs:14.
findings.reproduction: Compile mnemocode-wasm with --no-default-features --features browser-files, separately from the full card profile.
findings.expected: A documented isolated browser feature activates every directly imported dependency.
findings.observed: browser-files enables embroidery and sskr but not dep:mnemocode-cards. files.rs directly imports that crate; a transitive dependency does not provide its --extern.
findings.impact: The native isolated-feature check reproduced the unresolved dependency. The same source/feature closure applies to wasm32, whose separate target check was not run. Full profiles can hide the omission.
findings.recommendedFix: Activate the optional direct dependency or remove the direct import, with no unnecessary whole-module export.
findings.requiredVerification: Native/wasm32 isolated feature checks and the full intended profile after freezing the source.

findings.title: Library documentation has not caught up with the new browser file/share APIs
findings.reproduction: Compare the browser capability paragraph and feature table with the final reviewed API additions.
findings.expected: Documentation distinguishes newly supported file import/share creation from remaining typed-legend and host-integration gaps.
findings.observed: The guide still restricts browser embroidery to whole backups and omits browser-files, after those APIs were added during the audit.
findings.impact: Integrators cannot discover current capabilities or understand the actual remaining gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the feature table and API guide once the interfaces and gates are frozen.
findings.requiredVerification: Compile every documented feature independently and execute the listed minimal browser examples.

observations.title: Withdrawn: legacy prefix helper was tested against a stronger contract than documented
evidence: Local evidence: regression-harness-final.log, legacy-prefix-cli-corrected.log and legacy-prefix-explicit-length.log.
observations.reproduction: The audit test appended three decoys to a legacy backup and unwrapped shorter_phrases. A closing-CLI probe omitted --words; a control supplied --words 12.
observations.expected: The published helper contract permits propagating refusals; documented recovery with extra codes specifies the original length.
observations.observed: The assertion gets GivesSeveral, which the helper contract permits. CLI without --words returns an error after an invalid full-length checksum; with --words 12 it exits 0 and restores the original public phrase.
observations.impact: No failure of documented prefix recovery is established. The interactive caller could improve optional diagnostics rather than let their error bypass retry choices; this narrower UI path was not dynamically reproduced.
observations.recommendedFix: Do not count this assertion as a confirmed recovery defect. Consider a targeted interactive diagnostic/retry check before proposing a UI change.
observations.requiredVerification: A future interactive test must distinguish the primary invalid input from optional diagnostic failure and verify the documented explicit-length route.

observations.title: Kept's nested strings depend on the native-host allocator contract
observations.reproduction: Trace Kept and its nested String/Vec ownership and the documented ZeroingAllocator requirement.
observations.expected: Assess the supported host contract rather than assume an allocator configuration the library explicitly delegates to its host.
observations.observed: Kept redacts Debug but has no independent zeroizing Drop. The CLI and WASM register ZeroingAllocator; native-host general-allocation wiping is explicitly delegated to that allocator.
observations.impact: No separate secret-lifecycle violation was established within this reviewed contract. Directly protected nested buffers would reduce reliance on host setup.
observations.recommendedFix: Consider stronger local ownership as hardening; keep native-host obligations explicit.
observations.requiredVerification: If ownership changes, exercise nested allocation growth and drop under the supported host configuration.

limitations: This is a release-hold audit, not a clean acceptance certificate or proof that all defects were found.
Source changed concurrently. Findings bind to the listed exact file/diff snapshots; future edits require targeted re-verification.
Some findings have static call-path evidence only. Nine intentionally failing regression assertions and one public PTY reproduction distinguish executed failures from proposed reproductions.

The broad bounded CLI run hit its 1200-second wall limit during stitch_terminal after documented failures; remaining tests are not silently counted as passed. Two terminal isolation/cleanup tests were then run separately on freshly rebuilt closing source.
Automatic approval review rejected the full self-test because it conflicts with the exclusion of costly mass rendering. It was not run indirectly; two tests invoking it were skipped before execution.

Tests were frequently thermally paused at 90 C until cooling to 85 C; machine temperature sometimes exceeded the threshold between samples due to shared load. The longest run observed 100 C. Timing is not an application performance benchmark. Memory-headroom monitoring did not trigger an OOM or memory-pressure stop in the recorded jobs.
Small public-fixture PDF/QR tests ran; no exhaustive design/page/image matrix or hundreds of templates were generated.
Coverage percentages in COVERAGE.md remain historical (81.07% at its named older revision). No fresh full coverage percentage is claimed for the changed tree.
Only selected upstream implementation paths were inspected. The refreshed RustSec scan is advisory coverage, not an audit of all dependency code.

Native library hosts must register the documented zeroing allocator for general allocations. Kept/plain temporary copies are a hardening observation, not a demonstrated violation of that supported host contract.

Full cross-platform OS/terminal behavior, real browser UI/JS glue/CSP, physical QR print reliability, all wallet coins, Miri, fuzzing and IR/assembly zeroization validation remain outside newly executed checks.
No commit, push, release, model training, paid service or remote infrastructure mutation was performed.

environment.resourcePolicy: Per-job cgroup limit up to 6 GiB or available-minus-1.5 GiB; no swap allowance. Additional monitor stops its own job below 5% MemAvailable or sustained full PSI above 5. Thermal pause 90/resume85; maximum wall limits20m, final terminal scope5m.

executions.command:
bash -c 'set +e
bad=0
for args in "build --locked --offline -p mnemocode-cli" "xtask code-rules --self-test" "xtask code-rules" "xtask copies --self-test" "xtask copies" "xtask markdown" "xtask notices --check"; do

  cargo $args

  test "$rc" -eq 0 || bad=1
done
exit "$bad"'

notes: Superseded baseline candidates: missing WASM card import, absent share construction and obsolete LegacyLastWords export expectations were changed during review. They are not counted as current findings; remaining narrow API/feature defects are recorded.
No confirmed corruption follows merely from a high-density QR or long legend in this audit. Metadata merge/reorder/duplicate/conflict controls passed; full visual matrices were excluded.
Stale CLI tests are not application deadlocks. A failed old expectation of a mode marker must be migrated to the explicitly selected current mode.
One early source-gate attempt used a stale xtask binary with an old embedded root and was excluded. Freshly rebuilt xtask produced the recorded failures.

Three command metadata files initially suffered shell expansion in their recording wrapper. The exact issued command records were restored and marked; original execution logs and their hashes were unchanged.
The first CLI scope was stopped before its full-self-test integrations; the scoped rerun skipped those calls. Totals from overlapping runs are not added.
One interim source-gate failure was caused by the audit harness's standalone lint configuration. It was corrected in the harness and is not a production finding.
Independent challenge withdrew the prefix-helper assertion as a confirmed defect and downgraded explicit Debug disclosure to low. Both reconciliation decisions preserve the original failing evidence.

Two source-gate wrappers redirected only their final shell status test, leaving empty logs. Their observed tool output is not used as retained evidence; final-gates-retained reruns both gates with complete capture. An initial legacy-prefix CLI probe included a heading instead of just numeric codes; corrected probes are separately recorded.
